newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher ahead of USDA crop ratings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher ahead of USDA crop ratings.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended slightly higher in cautious trade ahead of Monday's USDA weekly crop updates that were expected to show a slight increase in corn condition ratings, traders said.

"I think it's just more of a wait-and-see kind of situation with today's crop conditions," Merrill Lynch grain analyst Randy Mittelstaedt said. "They will be the first ones to pick up the rains (last week)."
The trade was expecting a one- to two-percent improvement in the weekly crop ratings which will be released at 1500 CDT Monday.
The weekly report took on increased significance as the market tried to determine whether recent showers had improved crop conditions, traders said.
Weather Services Corp said weekend storms brought 1.0 to 2.5 inches of rain with 80 percent coverage across Illinois.

While most trade sources said the rains came too late to reverse crop damage done during the dry month of July, some suggested the moisture would aid in ear filling and lead to increased test weights.
Corn ended four to 3/4 cents per bushel higher with December up one at $2.63-1/2 a bushel.

Corn drew support from the National Weather Service 30-day outlook that suggested below normal temperatures in the U.S. Midwest in September. That forecast, combined with an early cold snap in Canada over the weekend, led to talk of an early frost, traders said.

Friday's USDA cattle on feed data was also mildly supportive to corn. USDA said July placements in the leading seven cattle-feeding states were estimated at 118 percent of a year ago, much higher than analysts had expected.
USDA weekly export inspections data was viewed as neutral. USDA said Monday there were 19,812,000 bushels of corn inspected for export in the week ended August 14.
That figure was below trade estimates for 24 to 28 million but traders noted last week's number was above expectations, meaning the two-week average was about as expected.

On the day, commercials were largely on the sell-side which traders linked to hedging activity. Cargill Inc sold three million bushels December and ADM sold 1.5 million December. Term Commodities and Farmers Commodities Corp were said to be buyers of the December.
Iowa Grain, Refco Inc, Lee B. Stern and Dean Witter each bought two million December, traders said.
Dean Witter also sold five million December, floor sources said, and Griffin Trading sold two million September while Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold two million December.

In options trade, Smith Barney bought 1,600 December $2.50 puts at 6-1/2 cents, Tenco Inc bought 500 September $2.60 calls at 2-1/2 to three cents and ADM sold 200 December $2.70 calls at 10 cents and $2.70 puts at 16-1/4, floor sources said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 49,087.
